summary.intent: Fix a broken statusline and Stop-hook error, update GSD to the latest version, clean up stale worktrees, then plan and fully execute phase 61 (AAD-Bound Seal Primitive and Cross-Language KAT) through to a shippable PR.
summary.outcome: All environment issues were resolved (statusline renamed to .cjs, GSD reinstalled to 1.6.0 restoring the missing hook), worktrees removed, and phase 61 was fully planned, implemented across 4 waves/5 plans, adversarially verified (including a third-implementation OpenSSL proof of the KAT ciphertext), and marked complete with 196 TS + 97 Rust tests green and a SHIP security verdict.

repo: package.json has "type": "module" — any hook written in CommonJS must use the .cjs extension; a .js file crashes with 'require is not defined in ES module scope' and silently blanks the statusline.
.claude/hooks/gsd-* is gitignored (.gitignore:55) — GSD hooks are installed locally via npx and not tracked; a fresh clone or partial install will silently lose them.
GSD package is @opengsd/gsd-core, installed via npx, gitignored. Reinstall command: npx @opengsd/gsd-core@<version> -- gsd-core --claude --local

vitest include is 'src/**/*.ts' — test files must live under packages/crypto/src/__tests__/, not packages/crypto/__tests__/. CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP (SC#3, TEST-02) had the wrong path; VALIDATION.md line 68 documents the deliberate correction.
scripts/check-vector-parity.sh has a hardcoded EXPECTED_VECTORS array — adding a new vector file (e.g. node-aad.json) is a required explicit CI integration task, not automatic.
sealAesGcmAad mints a fresh random IV on every call and cannot produce a fixed output; fixed-IV KAT vectors must target the lower-level encryptAesGcmAad / decrypt_aes_gcm_aad directly.
uuid crate was not in root Cargo.toml or crates/crypto/Cargo.toml — any new workspace dep needs two-line additions to both.
Phase 61 was purely additive (zero AAD consumers existed at time of implementation); no consumer rewiring was needed.
Pre-existing @types/node resolution failure exists in root tsconfig.scripts.json (types: ["node"] but @types/node not hoisted); not a regression surface for crypto changes.
1Password SSH signing requires biometric approval and will hang unattended commits — disable signing locally for AFK sessions; re-sign before merging if the repo enforces signatures on PRs.

code.finding: Referenced by settings.local.json for four hook events (including Stop) but was never installed into the main tree — only existed in now-removed worktrees. Restored by GSD 1.6.0 reinstall.
Renamed from statusline.js to force CommonJS mode; the repo's package.json type:module caused Node to treat the original as ESM, crashing on require() calls.
EXPECTED_VECTORS is a hardcoded bash array. node-aad.json was explicitly registered here in plan 61-01; any new vector file requires the same manual addition or the CI parity step fails.

New KAT fixture. Keyed structure with two arrays: aad_vectors (4 role-byte vectors) and seal_vectors (full-seal fixed-IV vector). aad_vectors role set must be asserted explicitly (expect length 4 + role set [1,2,3,4]) to prevent vacuous passes on future edits.
Correct TS KAT path — vitest include: ['src/**/*.ts'] means tests outside src/ are never discovered. Must include explicit toHaveLength(4) and role-set assertion on aad_vectors.
node_aad_cross_language test added; asserts Rust build_node_aad output is byte-identical to the committed node-aad.json vectors. assert_eq!(aad_vectors.len(), 4) pins role count.
Contains a Validation Architecture section — per GSD conventions this triggers creation of a VALIDATION.md for the phase.

Tracks two LOW security findings: (1) TS/Rust accept slightly different non-canonical UUID string forms (fail-closed but a parity gap); (2) uuidToBytes throws plain Error instead of CryptoError INVALID_AAD_INPUT for 32-char non-hex input.

workflow: GSD commit helper has a known false-negative pattern — it reports failure even when the commit succeeds. Always verify with git log rather than trusting the helper's exit status.

GSD plan-checker adversarial workflow (ultracode): spawning a canonical plan-checker plus multiple crypto-specific adversarial lenses in parallel, with an auto-revision round via the planner if blockers surface, converged in 2 rounds and caught a vacuous-pass hole that the single plan-checker alone might have missed.

KAT vector arrays require explicit length and content-set assertions (not just iteration) — a for...of over an empty array passes vacuously, silently eroding the coverage the phase was designed to freeze.

For sequential waves with cross-file dependencies (e.g. plan 02 reads a file written by plan 01), disable worktrees and run on the main tree with warm caches; worktree isolation adds overhead without parallelism benefit for single-plan-per-wave designs.

Post-implementation adversarial security review as a distinct step (separate from plan-checker) caught UUID acceptance-form parity divergence — a structural issue invisible to behavioral tests. For crypto code, a third-implementation verification (e.g. reproducing the KAT ciphertext via OpenSSL) is a strong correctness signal.
Pattern mapper independently re-confirmed all four research findings — running it as a separate subagent before the planner provides a useful redundancy check on research quality.
STATE.md automated update helper may silently no-op; always verify and hand-fix the Current Position before committing planning artifacts.

friction: Statusline silently went blank with no error surfaced to the user — the ESM crash happened inside the hook subprocess and was swallowed.
Stop hook error fired every single turn because settings.local.json referenced a file that was never installed in the main tree, producing noisy MODULE_NOT_FOUND spam throughout the session.

Main-tree GSD install was a broken fragment (no gsd-tools.cjs, no update.md, no file manifest) despite settings referencing managed hooks — the normal /gsd-update flow couldn't self-repair because the tooling it would invoke was missing.
GSD worktrees were on 1.4.3 while the gitignore comment pinned 1.6.0 — the install state was inconsistent across the repo.
Plan-phase round 1 had blockers requiring a full planner re-spawn (round 2) before the plan-checker passed — added latency to the planning pipeline.
GSD commit helper false-negatives required a git log verification step after every commit, adding friction throughout the session.

CONTEXT.md contained the wrong test path (packages/crypto/__tests__/ instead of packages/crypto/src/__tests__/), which was only caught by the researcher subagent — not by the discuss-phase that produced CONTEXT.md.
Pre-existing @types/node hoisting gap in root tsconfig.scripts.json caused a false-positive typecheck failure that required manual investigation to rule out as a regression.
STATE.md automated update helper silently no-oped, requiring a manual read + two-edit sequence to fix Current Position before the planning commit.
open_items: LOW-1 security finding: TS and Rust accept slightly different non-canonical UUID string forms (each rejects edge cases the other accepts). Tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-06-28-harden-uuid-acceptance-parity-aad-builder.md — needs a canonicalization policy decision before closing.
LOW-2 security finding: uuidToBytes throws plain Error instead of CryptoError INVALID_AAD_INPUT for 32-char non-hex input — contract inconsistency. Same todo file.
PR signature check will show red because commit signing was disabled for the AFK session. Needs re-sign/rebase before merging if the repo enforces signatures.
Pre-existing @types/node resolution failure in root tsconfig.scripts.json (scripts/*.ts typecheck broken independent of phase 61).
Branches fix/phase60-safety-tail and fix/fuse-delete-share-revocation still exist after worktree removal — may need cleanup or merging.

Consider extending generate-test-vectors.ts to auto-generate node-aad.json vectors rather than hand-freezing them (deferred per CONTEXT.md decision, recommended as follow-up after C-01 merge gate is green).
Phase 62 (Unified Node Codec) and phases 63-69 remain unstarted, all linearly gated behind phase 61's completion.
